name: Sudbury Neutrino Observatory

facility_roles.note: SNO occupied the original excavated cavern that SNOLAB (owned by the facilities workstream) later expanded around; referenced here, not created.

intervals.label: cavity excavation
intervals.quote: Mar 1990 -- Start of cavity excavation ... May 1993 -- End of cavity excavation

intervals.label: detector construction (clean room, acrylic vessel, PMT support, water fill)
intervals.quote: Nov 1994 -- Start of clean room assembly phase ... Apr 1999 -- Water fill complete

intervals.label: commissioning (first neutrinos)
intervals.quote: May 1999 -- First neutrinos found ... Nov 1999 -- Production data taking begins

intervals.label: phase 1: pure D2O
intervals.quote: Nov 1999 -- Production data taking begins ... May 2001 -- Start of 2nd phase of data taking (salt fill)

intervals.label: phase 2: NaCl-doped D2O (salt phase)
intervals.quote: May 2001 -- Start of 2nd phase of data taking (salt fill)
intervals.note: End date (salt removal, Sept 2003) per the awa/queensu milestones summary; the phase 3 start (Feb 2004) follows a several-month gap for NCD array installation.

intervals.label: phase 3: NCD array
intervals.quote: Feb 2004 -- Start of 3rd phase of data taking (with NCD detectors) ... Nov 2006 -- End of datataking for 3rd phase

intervals.label: shut down / drained
intervals.quote: Nov 2006 -- End of datataking for 3rd phase
intervals.note: D2O was drained from the acrylic vessel in May 2007, after which the cavern was converted for SNO+.

physics_goals.value: Detect solar neutrinos via charged-current, neutral-current and elastic-scattering reactions on heavy water to test the neutrino-oscillation solution to the solar neutrino problem in a solar-model-independent way
physics_goals.quote: a solar model-independent test of the neutrino oscillation hypothesis by comparison of the charged- and neutral-current interaction rates

unique_capabilities.value: A heavy-water (D2O) Cherenkov detector, uniquely sensitive to the neutral-current reaction that counts all active solar-neutrino flavours, not just electron neutrinos
unique_capabilities.quote: Observations of neutral current neutrino interactions on deuterium in the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory are reported.

quantity.quote: The center of the detector vessel is 2039 m below the surface in a cavity excavated from the "6800-foot" level of the mine.
quantity.note: Same source already cited by facility:snolab's site record (site:snolab-underground-lab), re-verified directly in this session.

summary.plain: A detector two kilometres underground in a Canadian nickel mine, filled with 1000 tonnes of heavy water, that solved the decades-old mystery of the Sun's missing neutrinos by showing they change type on the way to Earth.
summary.technical: Heavy-water Cherenkov solar-neutrino detector 2039 m underground in Vale's Creighton mine, Sudbury, Ontario, run 1999-2006 in three phases (pure D2O; NaCl-doped D2O; D2O with an array of neutral-current detectors). Its neutral-current measurement gave solar-model-independent, direct evidence of solar neutrino flavour transformation.
